paper_title: PM-KVQ Progressive Mixed-precision KV Cache Quantization for Long-CoT   LLMs
caption: : DeepSeek-R1-Distill-QwQ-32B

model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity of 4-bit and 2-bit quantized key-value (KV) cache blocks across different block indices for the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-QwQ-32B model, as part of the PM-KVQ progressive mixed-precision quantization framework. The horizontal axis, labeled “Block Index,” ranges from 0 to 63, with tick marks at intervals of 15 (i.e., 0, 15, 31, 47, 63), indicating discrete blocks in the KV cache. The vertical axis, labeled “Sensitivity,” is logarithmic, spanning from approximately 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴, with major gridlines at each decade and minor ticks dividing the scale into finer increments. Two sets of bars are shown for each block index: green bars represent the 2-bit quantization scheme, and blue bars represent the 4-bit scheme, as indicated in the legend in the top-left corner. For block indices from 0 to approximately 18, only green bars are present, indicating that 2-bit quantization is used for these blocks, with sensitivities typically between 10⁻⁵ and 10⁻⁵.5. Starting at block index ~19, both green and blue bars appear, with the blue bars (4-bit) consistently higher than the green bars (2-bit) in sensitivity, indicating that 4-bit quantization is more sensitive for these blocks. From block index ~31 onward, the blue bars become increasingly dominant, and by block index ~47 to 63, only blue bars are shown, suggesting that 4-bit quantization is applied exclusively to these later blocks. The sensitivity of the 4-bit blocks increases progressively, peaking around index 61–63 with values approaching or exceeding 10⁻⁴. This visual progression reflects a progressive mixed-precision strategy where lower-precision quantization (2-bit) is applied to less sensitive early blocks, while higher-precision (4-bit) is reserved for more sensitive later blocks in the sequence, optimizing memory and computation without significant performance degradation.
model_annotations.German: The bar chart illustrates the sensitivity of different quantization schemes—4-Fbit (blue bars) and 2-Fbit (green bars)—across 64 blocks, indexed from 0 to 63, in the context of the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-QwQ-32B model. The horizontal axis, labeled "Block Index," is linearly scaled and marked at intervals of 15 (0, 15, 31, 47, 63), indicating the position of each block in the model. The vertical axis, labeled "Sensitivity," uses a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 10⁻⁵ to 10⁻⁴, with tick marks at regular logarithmic intervals. For each block index, two adjacent bars represent the sensitivity values for the 4-Fbit and 2-Fbit quantization methods, respectively. The green bars (2-Fbit) are consistently shorter than the blue bars (4-Fbit) across most block indices, indicating lower sensitivity for the 2-Fbit scheme. Notably, the sensitivity values for both schemes are relatively low and stable across the first 30 blocks, with a gradual increase observed from block 31 onward. The 4-Fbit sensitivity values rise more sharply, particularly from block 47 to 63, where the blue bars reach the upper end of the scale (near 10⁻⁴), while the green bars remain below 10⁻⁵. The bars are arranged in groups of two per block index, with no explicit sorting or emphasis on any particular block, and the legend in the top-left corner clearly distinguishes the two quantization methods by color.
